To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CD44s expression is down‐regulated with malignant transformation of colon mucosa.
CD44s expression in colon‐carcinomas influences growth of metastases.
the expression of a CD44s isoform in a colon carcinoma cell line reduces its ability to establish experimental liver‐metastasis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of cell adhesion in cancer metastasis.
the role of the cell adhesion molecule CD44s in human colon carcinogenesis.
understanding the role of the CD44s isoform in human colon carcinogenesis, and the role of the hyaluronan binding site in the development of experimental liver metastasis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression of CD44s in human colon carcinomass influences the growth of liver metastasis.
CD44s plays an important role in colon cancer metastasis.
CD44s expression is associated with reduced growth of experimental liver colon carcinoma metastases, and this may be a consequence of CD44s‐mediated cell–matrix interactions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CD44s is a negative regulator for colon carcinoma liver metastasis.
down‐regulation or loss of CD44s, which occurs during malignant transformation of colomic mucosa, is a key factor in the development of liver metastases from colon cancer.
the expression of CD44s is associated with a reduced ability of human colon carcinomatous cells to grow in liver metastases.
The main takeaway from our work is that

CD44s expression in colon carcinomas influences the growth of liver metastasis, but that the influence of CD4s expression on the growth of liver metasatases is not dependent on the binding of CD44s to hyaluronan.

down‐regulation (or loss) of CD44s in colon carcinomas can enhance growth of experimental metastases, and therefore, the functional consequences associated with loss of CD44s may be just as important as the consequences of CD44 up‐regulation.

the functional consequences of down‐regulation (loss) of CD44s in human colon carcinogenesis are just as significant as are the functional consequences of up‐regulated expression of high‐molecualr‐weight CD44v isoforms.
